name: DFS Trees
description: You are given a connected undirected graph consisting of $$$n$$$ vertices and $$$m$$$ edges. The weight of the $$$i$$$-th edge is $$$i$$$. Here is a wrong algorithm of finding a minimum spanning tree (MST) of a graph: vis := an array of length n s := a set of edges function dfs(u): vis[u] := true iterate through each edge (u, v) in the order from smallest to largest edge weight if vis[v] = false add edge (u, v) into the set (s) dfs(v) function findMST(u): reset all elements of (vis) to false reset the edge set (s) to empty dfs(u) return the edge set (s) Each of the calls findMST(1) , findMST(2) , ..., findMST(n) gives you a spanning tree of the graph. Determine which of these trees are minimum spanning trees.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains two integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$ ($$$2\le n\le 10^5$$$, $$$n-1\le m\le 2\cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of vertices and the number of edges in the graph. Each of the following $$$m$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$ ($$$1\le u_i, v_i\le n$$$, $$$u_i\ne v_i$$$), describing an undirected edge $$$(u_i,v_i)$$$ in the graph. The $$$i$$$-th edge in the input has weight $$$i$$$. It is guaranteed that the graph is connected and there is at most one edge between any pair of vertices.
output_specification: You need to output a binary string $$$s$$$, where $$$s_i=1$$$ if findMST(i) creates an MST, and $$$s_i = 0$$$ otherwise.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1707C — DFS Trees [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
